name: Service request
blurb: Four lines: a prose condition and an extraction. One pass on one request.
input: Hi, could you please reset my password today? I can't get into the app. Email me when it's done.
expect: a service request; urgency now and channel email are extracted from the same pass

name: Support triage
blurb: A kind and a scale, a switch with case unsure, and one settle() that decides what counts as sure.
input: I was charged twice last month and I want that money back now. This is the third time.
expect: a refund from someone at least annoyed on Mood: logs "refund, escalate"

name: Status update
blurb: A shape with kinded and text slots: decisions fill the first, a chat model writes the second.
input: Any news on the outage ticket I raised for the billing dashboard yesterday? Still can't see invoices.
expect: asks for a status update; the Ticket's topic comes from the same pass, its product and summary from the chat model, and a two-sentence acknowledgement is logged

name: Intent router
blurb: The platform's regex router rewritten: the mention-versus-ask hazard becomes one prose predicate.
input: translate 'my card was declined' into Spanish
expect: { mode: "chat", via: "model" }: the quoted decline is no action to take, and a translation is answerable from knowledge alone

name: Review sweep
blurb: parallel over a list under a pass budget; each review costs one pass.
input: ["The courier was rude and slammed the door.", "Lovely product, arrived early.", "Sam at the desk ignored us for ten minutes.", "Late, but the coffee machine itself is fine."]
expect: one pass per review in parallel; the cold review naming Sam at the desk is flagged, and the count of flagged reviews is logged

name: Support desk
blurb: decide, extract, a chat reply, a guardrail question about that reply, a person's yes, and a tool that files the ticket.
input: My invoice was charged twice and I need it fixed today
expect: a support issue; a short reply streamed; on yes a ticket id

name: Order assistant
blurb: An assistant that picks its own tools; the refund tool asks a person first, and a predicate with unless guards against a claimed refund.
input: Where is A-1234? And refund it, it is late
expect: the lookup runs, the person is asked, the reply states what happened

name: Inbox sweep
blurb: parallel over a JSON list, one pass each, a kind and a scale together, tolerate, all under settle({ passes: 200 }).
input: ["You charged me twice and nobody has answered in a week.", "Where is my order A-2000?", "Thanks, the new dashboard is lovely.", "Unsubscribe me from this list.", "The app crashes every time I open invoices.", "Do you ship to Ireland?", "Your courier left the parcel in the rain. Furious.", "Great support today, thank you Sam.", "Delivery notification: parcel returned to sender.", "How do I change the card on my account?", "I have been on hold for forty minutes.", "Loved the packaging, five stars.", "Please cancel my subscription before the renewal.", "Is there a student discount?", "Third time asking: where is my refund?", "Out of office: I am away until Monday.", "The invoice PDF will not open.", "Can you explain the new pricing?", "Brilliant, arrived a day early.", "Win a free holiday, click here now."]
expect: 20 passes in parallel; counts by action

name: Doc Q&A
blurb: A memory taught with "remember: …", recalled into a prompt, and a question that checks the answer stayed inside the passages.
input: remember: Vacation: 25 days a year, booked two weeks ahead.
expect: teach then ask → an answer citing [1]

name: Moderator
blurb: One yes/no question with an unsure branch that asks a person; unattended, the post waits in a memory and the counts live in another.
input: Everyone on the support team is a useless idiot who should be fired.
expect: clear posts in one pass; borderline asks or holds
